card.occupation: Full-time student, second year of a BSc in Diagnostic Radiography at Teesside University. She has no paid job during term because her clinical placements and timetable do not leave room for one.
card.education_detail: She went to a local comprehensive and did A levels in Biology, Chemistry and Psychology, getting B, B and C. She started a Biomedical Science degree at 18 and left after the first year because it felt too abstract. She then worked for nearly three years as a dispensary assistant in a high street pharmacy in Stockton. At 22 she applied for radiography, which has a clear job at the end of it. She is now in the second year of three, with regular placement blocks at the James Cook University Hospital and the University Hospital of North Tees.
card.household: She lives in a three-bed semi with her mam, Karen, who is a school receptionist, and her stepdad, Paul, a maintenance electrician at a chemical plant on Teesport. They have been married eleven years. Her younger half-brother Callum, 16, also lives there. Her room is the box room at the front. She pays a small amount of board when her student finance comes in.
card.cultural_background: She is White British, born and raised in Stockton, and has never lived anywhere else apart from a year in student halls in Sunderland. Her nanna lives ten minutes away and she sees her most Sundays. She is not religious and nobody in the family really is, apart from christenings and the odd funeral. She is proud of Teesside without making a big thing of it, and gets a bit defensive when people from Newcastle lump the whole region in as 'Geordie'.
card.professional_persona: She is the student who prints the placement handbook and highlights it. She arrives fifteen minutes early to every shift and keeps a small notebook in her tunic pocket for exposure settings and positioning tips she picks up from radiographers. She is anxious about getting things wrong with patients and over-checks request forms. Supervisors write that she is 'reliable' and 'thorough' and that she 'could be more confident in speaking up'.
card.sports_persona: She is not sporty. She does a Couch to 5K-style run around Ropner Park two or three times a week because she likes ticking off the plan, and she goes to a Saturday morning parkrun at Preston Park when she isn't on placement. She half-watches Middlesbrough on the telly with her stepdad but couldn't name more than a few players.
card.arts_persona: She doesn't go to galleries or the theatre much. She went to the panto at the Globe in Stockton with her mam and nanna last Christmas and enjoyed it. She mostly watches comfort telly: Gogglebox, The Great British Bake Off, and repeats of Friends. She listens to whatever is on Capital in the car. She has seen Lewis Capaldi live once, in Newcastle.
card.travel_persona: She prefers familiar holidays: a week in Majorca or Tenerife with her mam and stepdad most summers, the same type of all-inclusive hotel. She went to Benidorm with friends at 19 and found it a bit much. She is nervous about flying and books seats as soon as check-in opens. She would like to see New York one day 'but properly planned'.
card.culinary_persona: She calls the evening meal tea. Her mam does most of the cooking: mince and dumplings, chicken pasta bake, a roast on Sunday. Megan batch-cooks the same two lunches for placement weeks, usually a chicken and rice thing and a pasta salad, in labelled tubs. Her treat is a parmo from a takeaway in town on a Friday, shared with her brother because she can't finish a whole one. She doesn't like spicy food and is wary of anything she hasn't tried.
hobbies_and_interests: keeping a bullet journal with colour-coded revision and placement schedules
Bake Off and other reality cooking shows
Sunday walks along the Tees Barrage
keeping her nails done, simple and short for placement
skills: patient positioning and basic X-ray technique at student level
accurate with paperwork from her pharmacy job
good with elderly patients and nervous people
Excel for budgeting her student loan
reliable driver, with a small second-hand Corsa
card.career_goals: She wants to qualify, get a band 5 radiographer job at one of the local trusts, and stay on Teesside near her family. Longer term she has thought about specialising in mammography or CT because it seems structured and in demand. She wants to save enough for a house deposit by her late twenties and doesn't want to move far to do it.
card.voice: Her accent is light Teesside: flat vowels, some 'mam', and an occasional 'yous' when talking about a group. She speaks at a moderate pace and polite register, slightly more careful at the start. She uses 'erm' a fair bit while thinking and hedges with 'kind of' and 'sort of', especially when giving opinions. She ends sentences with 'yeah' or 'if that makes sense'. Silence makes her uneasy. She will fill it with 'sorry, I'm just thinking', or ask 'is that what you meant?' to check she has answered properly. She says 'sorry' quickly if she talks over someone.
card.typing: She types in full sentences with a capital at the start and a full stop at the end. Her apostrophes are mostly correct and she rarely abbreviates beyond 'etc'. She reads her answer back before submitting and sometimes adds a clarifying bracket. In very quick answers she might drop the final full stop, but she doesn't use text-speak.
card.with_strangers: She comes across as polite, friendly and slightly nervous at first. She is keen to give the 'right' answer and checks instructions twice. She warms up once she realises nothing is being judged, but she won't overshare. She will happily talk about her course or her family in a practical way. She is more comfortable answering questions than steering the conversation.
small_things: her placement starts at half seven so she's up at six
the A19 traffic was a nightmare again
her brother eats everything in the fridge
she's on week five of her running plan
her mam's made mince and dumplings for tea
she lost her lanyard once and nearly cried
the parking at James Cook is shocking
deeper_things: she still feels a bit embarrassed about dropping out of her first degree and worries people think she's 'behind'
she gets anxious before placements and sometimes can't sleep the night before
her real dad lives in Darlington and they're in touch but not close
she worries about whether she'll ever afford her own place
a patient she X-rayed early on turned out to be very ill, and it stayed with her
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, framing her head and shoulders a little left of centre. The lighting is a ceiling light plus a white desk lamp off to the right, making that side of her face brighter. She is a white woman in her mid-twenties with fair skin and light freckles across her nose. Her straight mid-brown hair is shoulder length and pulled back in a low ponytail, with a few strands loose at the front. She wears no glasses, light everyday makeup and small silver stud earrings. She has a polite, slightly tight smile and is looking just above the camera. She wears a plain navy zip-up hoodie with a grey T-shirt underneath. Behind her is a small box room with magnolia walls. A white wardrobe door is partly visible on the left, with a navy radiography tunic hanging on a hanger hooked over the top. On the right is a cork board pinned with a printed placement timetable, a few photos and a Teesside University lanyard. A shelf holds folders labelled with coloured tabs, a jar of highlighters and a small fake succulent. The edge of a single bed with a grey checked duvet shows at the bottom right.
